As we wrap up our time with the rocket boys of Coalwood, I hope you’re walking away with more than just a story about rockets and science fairs.
What we’ve really witnessed is the slow, sometimes tough, but always hopeful journey of growing up—of learning to trust yourself, to lean on your friends and family, and to keep moving forward, even when you can’t quite see what’s ahead.
The lessons from Coalwood? They’re not stuck in the past. They matter just as much today.
So here’s what I want you to remember:
Perseverance isn’t about never facing setbacks—it’s built through them.
Community can turn what feels impossible into something you can actually achieve.
Family love might be quiet, but it shapes every dream you chase.
Hope is a choice, especially when the future feels uncertain.
And that first leap of courage to dream? That’s where real change begins.
Life throws all kinds of challenges at us—sometimes, it can make your biggest dreams feel totally out of reach. But the rocket boys showed us that if you’ve got determination, support from those around you, and the guts to keep trying—even when you fail—ordinary people can do some pretty extraordinary things.
You don’t need perfect circumstances, or endless resources. What matters most is that spark of curiosity, a willingness to work together, and the belief that what you’re doing matters.
So, as you head into your own crossroads—at work, with family, or just in those quiet moments when you’re doubting yourself—hang on to these lessons.
Let Coalwood’s story remind you: every journey is made of small steps, every setback is a chance to learn, and the sky is never as far away as it looks.
Keep looking up. The next chapter? It’s yours to write.
